summary: CCC-built 60-foot steel fire tower on Doe Mountain in Cherokee National Forest, restored in 2019 and reached by trail; the register's 1948 build date conflicts with 1936.

facts.design: 60-foot galvanized steel tower, Aermotor MC-39 standard plan

access.note: Reached on foot or by ATV on Doe Mountain Recreation Area trails. Clio says Multi-Use Trail 25 is the only way to visit the site.

visit.trail_note: A 2021 visit report describes a 4.5-mile hike up from the North Entrance of the park.

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps. The register gives 1948.
The Kingsport Times reported in August 1933 that a Kettle Foot fire tower would soon be built in the Holston and Iron Mountain section
Tennessee Division of Forestry stopped using it for fire lookout work in the mid-1970s, per Clio
On the National Register of Historic Places; the NPS record is dated 11/20/2015
Recently restored, according to a 2021 visit report

corrections.why: The NRHP nomination and the Clio summary both say the Civilian Conservation Corps built the tower in 1936. The register's 1948 has no cited source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1948. The NRHP nomination and Clio both date construction to 1936, and the 1933 newspaper item shows it was planned before 1948.

notes_for_editor: Build year is the one real conflict. The register says 1948, while the NRHP nomination and Clio say 1936 and the 1933 newspaper item shows it was planned earlier; a correction to 1936 is proposed for human review. Staffing is not recorded: the register's visit page reads 'Staffed? No', but that line is split and was not quoted. The NRHP period of significance ends in 1965, while Clio says the Tennessee Division of Forestry used it until the mid-1970s; the two describe different things and both are noted. The register names the Tennessee Division of Forestry as administrator, but the nomination places the tower inside Cherokee National Forest on Fire Tower Road. The register gives 3,885 feet while the NRHP nomination gives 3,889. The NRHP gives 60 feet. Clio says trail and tower repair plans were in the works, so current conditions may have changed since the 2021 visit. The register's 1948 may come from a later rebuild or a transcription error; the sources read do not say which.
